chapters.summary: In this chapter: looking for the furry cat; looking, hiding and finding; our national flag; chhuk chhuk goes our train.

lessons.title: Looking for the Furry Cat

activities.prompt: Where might the furry cat be hiding?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Follow the Cat Clues
activities.body: This poem is a playful hunt for the furry cat. It tells you to keep looking and asks about the window, the bed, the red rack and the backpack. It also gives clues from a jar, a car, a mat and a hat. Top means high, while bottom means low. Below means under, and above means over. At last, the poem says that the furry cat has come.
keyPoints: Keep looking for the furry cat.
The poem gives clues about many places.
At last, the furry cat has come.
activities.explanation: The poem moves through cat clues until the furry cat appears.

activities.prompt: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar. A child hears a scratching sound there. Where might the furry cat have been?
steps: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar.
The sound is at the bottom of the jar, so it matches that action.
Therefore, the furry cat may have been at the jar.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Under the Bed
activities.prompt: The poem asks if the cat is sleeping under the bed.
activities.explanation: Yes. The poem asks if the cat is sleeping under the bed.

activities.title: Inside the Backpack
activities.prompt: The poem asks if the cat is inside the ______.
activities.hint: This is a bag that you can carry.
activities.explanation: The poem asks if the cat is inside the backpack.

activities.title: Match the Cat Clues
activities.prompt: Match each place with its cat clue.
activities.explanation: Each place matches the action or position asked about in the poem.

activities.title: Where Was the Cat?
activities.prompt: Where was the cat scratching?
options: at the top of the car
at the bottom of the jar
activities.explanation: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar.

activities.title: Above or Below?
activities.prompt: The poem says the cat was hopping below the mat.
activities.explanation: The cat was hopping above the hat. It was hiding below the mat.

activities.title: Follow the Poem
activities.prompt: Put these cat clues in the order they appear in the poem.
items: Keep looking for the furry cat
Ask if the cat is on the window
Ask if the cat is under the bed
activities.explanation: The poem asks you to keep looking before it says that the cat has come.

activities.title: The Cat Appears
activities.prompt: What does the poem finally say?
options: The cat is looking for you
The cat is going to sleep
activities.explanation: The poem says that the furry cat has come.

activities.prompt: The furry cat is 6 cm above the hat, while the mat is 3 cm below the hat. How many cm farther above the hat is the cat than the mat is below it?
activities.explanation: The cat's distance above the hat is 6 cm. The mat's distance below the hat is 3 cm. To compare the distances, subtract the smaller distance from the larger one. 6 - 3 = 3 cm.
steps: The cat's distance above the hat is 6 cm.
The mat's distance below the hat is 3 cm.
To compare the distances, subtract the smaller distance from the larger one.
activities.hint: Compare the two distances and subtract the smaller distance.

steps: The cat's distance above the hat is {a} cm.
The mat's distance below the hat is {b} cm.

{a} - {b} = {answer} cm.

activities.prompt: A child starts at the window and walks 3 cm to the bed, then 3 cm to the outside red rack. The child then walks 3 cm back toward the window. How far from the window is the child now, in cm?
activities.explanation: The child starts at the window. The distance walked away from the window is 6 cm, found by adding the first two parts of the journey. The child then walks 3 cm back toward the window. 6 - 3 = 3 cm.
steps: The child starts at the window.
The distance walked away from the window is 6 cm, found by adding the first two parts of the journey.
The child then walks 3 cm back toward the window.
activities.hint: First find the total distance walked away from the window.

The distance walked away from the window is {forward} cm, found by adding the first two parts of the journey.

activities.prompt: You looked at the window. The furry cat was not there. What should you do next?
options: Keep looking in the places the poem names.
Stop looking because the furry cat cannot come.
Wait inside and do not look again.
Look under the bed only, then stop.

why.Stop looking because the furry cat canno: This mistakes one empty place for proof that the cat cannot come.
This wrongly waits instead of checking more places.
This wrongly treats one hiding place as the only place.

activities.explanation: The poem says to keep looking, so the search should continue.

activities.prompt: A child hears scratching at the bottom of a jar. What can we say about the furry cat?
options: The furry cat may have been at the bottom of the jar.
The furry cat is sleeping under the bed today.
The furry cat is hiding below the mat today.
The furry cat has come back to the jar today.

why.The furry cat is sleeping under the bed: The poem only asks about sleeping under the bed, not confirms it.
why.The furry cat is hiding below the mat to: The poem says it hid below the mat, but not that it stays.
why.The furry cat has come back to the jar t: The poem says it came, but not that it came back.

activities.explanation: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar.

lessons.title: Looking, Hiding and Finding

activities.prompt: Where is the ball hiding, and how can we help it find its way?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Look, Describe and Find
activities.body: Look carefully at each picture. You can talk about what you see and where things are. Words such as above, below, on and under help you describe positions. The book uses cats, dogs and cows in questions about position. You can hide things, give directions and throw a ball into a basket. Inside and outside tell you what happens to the ball.
keyPoints: Look carefully and tell what you see.
Use words to describe where things are.
Say IN or OUT when the ball goes in or out.
activities.explanation: These words help you look closely and describe where things are.

activities.title: Where is the ball?

tasks.say: Now put it under the table.
tasks.then: Under means below, hidden beneath.

tasks.say: Throw the ball IN the basket.
tasks.then: In: the ball is inside the basket.

tasks.say: Now it is OUT of the basket.
tasks.then: Out: the ball is outside the basket.

activities.takeaway: Position words say where something is: above, on, under, near, in and out.
activities.explanation: Position words say where something is: above, on, under, near, in and out.

activities.prompt: A child throws a ball. It goes inside a basket. What should the child say, and why?
steps: The ball went into the basket, so it is inside.
The school word for inside is IN.
The child says IN because the ball went inside the basket.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What can you do when you look at the pictures?
activities.explanation: Look carefully at each picture. Then tell another child what you can see.

activities.prompt: The book mentions cats, dogs and cows.
activities.explanation: Yes. These animals help you talk about where things are.

activities.prompt: Which pair is matched in one book question?
activities.explanation: Your book asks where the red ball is in relation to the bed.

activities.prompt: Match each thing to the other thing used with it.
activities.explanation: Each pair appears in a question about where one thing is.

activities.prompt: Players use words like inside, outside, near and ______ to give directions.
activities.hint: This word tells you that something is higher.
activities.explanation: Above is one of the words players use to give directions.

activities.prompt: The same team hides and finds the hidden things.
activities.explanation: One team hides things. Another team finds them.

activities.prompt: Put the ball steps in order.
items: say IN if it goes inside
activities.explanation: You aim first, then throw. Say IN when the ball goes inside.

activities.prompt: The ball goes outside the basket. What do children say?
activities.explanation: Children say OUT when the ball goes outside the basket.

activities.prompt: A picture shows a cat above a car. What is the cat's position relative to the car, and why?
options: The cat is above the car because the picture shows it there.
The cat is below the car because the picture shows it there.
The cat is inside the car because the picture shows it there.
The cat is outside the car because the picture shows it there.

why.The cat is below the car because the pic: This mixes up above and below.
why.The cat is inside the car because the pi: This mistakes a place above for a place inside.
why.The cat is outside the car because the p: This mistakes a place above for a place outside.

activities.explanation: This is right because the cat is above the car.

activities.prompt: A red ball rests on a bed. What is the red ball's position relative to the bed, and why?
options: The red ball is on the bed because it rests there.
The red ball is under the bed because it rests there.
The red ball is inside the bed because it rests there.
The red ball is outside the bed because it rests there.

why.The red ball is inside the bed because i: This mistakes resting on for being inside.
why.The red ball is outside the bed because: This mistakes resting on for being outside.

activities.explanation: This is right because the red ball rests on the bed.

lessons.title: Our National Flag

activities.prompt: What makes our national flag so special?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet the Tiranga
activities.body: The National Flag is also called tiranga. Your book asks how many colours it has. It asks which colour is at the top, below white and above green. Another question asks where the ashoka chakra is. Children discuss when, where and why the flag is hoisted. They express feelings about National celebrations. They make their own tiranga and sing the National Anthem while standing and facing the tiranga.
keyPoints: The National Flag is also called tiranga.
Your book asks about colours and the ashoka chakra.
Children discuss hoisting, celebrations, making and singing.
activities.explanation: This card introduces the tiranga and the questions in your book.

activities.prompt: The class is getting ready to sing the National Anthem. What should they make and do?
steps: The class should make their own tiranga because the book asks children to make one.
The class should sing the National Anthem because the book asks children to sing it.
They should stand and face the tiranga because that is how children sing.
So the clear plan is to make a tiranga and sing while facing it.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What other name does your book use?
activities.explanation: Great work! Tiranga is another name for the National Flag.

activities.prompt: The book asks which colour is above the green colour.
activities.explanation: Yes! Finding the colour above green is one of the book's questions.

activities.prompt: Your book asks where the ______ chakra is on the tiranga.
activities.hint: This word comes before the word 'chakra'.
activities.explanation: Well done! The book asks where the ashoka chakra is placed.

activities.prompt: What should children discuss about the National Flag?
options: what colours it has and where
when, where and why it is hoisted
how children can fold it safely
activities.explanation: Yes! Children discuss when, where and why the flag is hoisted.

activities.prompt: Children sing while standing with their backs to the tiranga.
activities.explanation: Good try! Children sing while standing and facing the tiranga.

activities.prompt: Put these questions in the order shown on page 6.
items: How many colours does the tiranga have?
Which colour is at the top?
activities.explanation: Wonderful! These questions appear in this order on page 6.

activities.prompt: What should children do when they sing the National Anthem?
options: Sing while standing and facing away.
Sit and sing while facing the tiranga.
Sing while standing and facing the tiranga.
Sing while standing and facing a book.
activities.explanation: You got it! Children stand and face the tiranga while singing.

activities.prompt: Each of 3 children colours all 3 colours on one tiranga. How many colour sections do they colour altogether?
activities.explanation: There are 3 children, and each child colours 3 sections. We need all the colour sections, so multiply the number of children by the number of sections each child colours. 3 x 3 = 9 colour sections altogether.
steps: There are 3 children, and each child colours 3 sections.
We need all the colour sections, so multiply the number of children by the number of sections each child colours.
3 x 3 = 9 colour sections altogether.
activities.hint: Multiply the number of children by the number of colours each child uses.

steps: There are {n} children, and each child colours {colours} sections.
We need all the colour sections, so multiply the number of children by the number of sections each child colours.
{n} x {colours} = {answer} colour sections altogether.
gen.hint: Multiply the number of children by the number of colours each child uses.

activities.prompt: A child writes “tiranga” on a National Flag drawing. What does this tell us?
options: These words name the same flag.
These words name two different flags.
Only one word names the National Flag.
These words name the National Anthem.

It wrongly treats the two names as different flags.
It wrongly thinks one name does not belong to the flag.
It wrongly swaps the flag and the anthem.

activities.explanation: Both words name the same National Flag.

lessons.title: Chhuk Chhuk Goes Our Train

activities.prompt: What will our train see on its journey today?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Our Train
activities.body: A train goes with a chhuk-chhuk sound. It goes over hills and down to the plains. It also goes over rivers and in the rain. Bogies make a chain. Some bogies come before another bogie, and some come after it. We can discuss what a train is and share our train journeys.
keyPoints: The train makes a chhuk-chhuk sound.
Bogies make a chain.
Some bogies come before or after another bogie.
activities.explanation: A train has many special parts, and each part helps us learn about it.

activities.prompt: Blue bogies are before red. Orange bogies are after it. What should the child colour?
steps: Find the red bogie in the chain, because both colour rules use it.
Colour the blue bogies before it, because blue must be coloured before red.
Colour the orange bogies after it, because orange must be coloured after red.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Train Sound
activities.prompt: What sound does the train go with?
activities.explanation: The train goes with a chhuk-chhuk sound. Well done!

activities.title: Colour the Bogies
activities.prompt: Which bogies must you colour after the red bogie?
activities.explanation: Children must colour the orange bogies after the red bogie.

activities.title: Make a Chain
activities.prompt: The bogies make a ______.
activities.hint: The bogies join together.
activities.explanation: The bogies make a chain.

activities.title: What Children Count
activities.prompt: Which question are children asked?
options: How many boats come after the engine?
How many bogies come after the engine?
How many bogies come before the engine?
How many red bogies come after the engine?
activities.explanation: Children are asked how many bogies come after the engine.

activities.title: Choose the Correct Colouring
activities.prompt: Which pair of colouring tasks is correct?
options: Orange bogies after red; blue bogies before red
Orange bogies before red; blue bogies after red
Green bogies after red; blue bogies before red
Orange bogies after blue; red bogies before blue
activities.explanation: Orange bogies come after the red bogie, and blue bogies come before it.

activities.prompt: A train has 2 bogies before the red bogie and 6 bogies after it. How many more bogies come after the red bogie than before it?
activities.explanation: The after group has 6 bogies. The before group has 2 bogies. Take the smaller number from the larger number: 6 - 2 = 4. There are 4 more bogies after the red bogie.
steps: The after group has 6 bogies.
The before group has 2 bogies.
Take the smaller number from the larger number: 6 - 2 = 4.
There are 4 more bogies after the red bogie.
activities.hint: Find the difference between the after group and the before group.

Take the smaller number from the larger number: {after} - {before} = {answer}.
There are {answer} more bogies after the red bogie.

There are 3 carriages before the red carriage.

There are 1 more carriages after the red carriage.

activities.prompt: The train is going over hills. What will it do next on its journey?
options: Go up and stay on the hills.
Stay on top of the hills.

This misses the train's path down to the plains.
This keeps the train from going down to the plains.
This misses both the hills and the plains.

activities.explanation: The train goes over hills and down to the plains.

activities.prompt: A red bogie has blue bogies before it. It has orange bogies after it. What should the child colour?
options: The blue bogies before red and the orange bogies after red.
The blue bogies after red and the orange bogies before red.
Every blue bogie and every orange bogie on the train.
Only the red bogie and no other bogies at all.

why.The blue bogies after red and the orange: This swaps the before and after colour rules.
why.Every blue bogie and every orange bogie: This colours all coloured bogies, not only the asked groups.
why.Only the red bogie and no other bogies a: This ignores both required colour groups.

activities.explanation: Blue goes before red, and orange goes after it.

activities.prompt: A child counts the engine again. The classmate calls this the count after the engine. Is the classmate right?
options: No. Count only the bogies that come after the engine.
Yes. Count the engine with the bogies after it.
No. Count only the bogies before the engine.
Yes. Stop counting as soon as the engine is found.

why.Yes. Count the engine with the bogies af: This puts the engine inside the group of bogies.
why.No. Count only the bogies before the eng: This uses the group before the engine instead.
why.Yes. Stop counting as soon as the engine: This thinks finding the engine finishes the count.

activities.explanation: The count must use only the bogies that come after the engine.

activities.prompt: A child says, "The bogies before the red bogie are after it." What should the child do?
options: Check the chain and count the bogies before red.
Change the chain so the red bogie is first.
Count the bogies after the red bogie instead.
Keep the claim because before means after.

why.Change the chain so the red bogie is fir: Changing the chain hides the mistake about before.
why.Count the bogies after the red bogie ins: This counts the wrong group for the red bogie.
why.Keep the claim because before means afte: This accepts before and after as the same.

activities.explanation: The claim swaps the group, so the child must count before red.

lessons.title: The Train Game

activities.prompt: Can we join together, sing, and play a train game?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Join the Train
activities.body: Children sing a rhyme that says, “Here goes our train”. They play a game, and all form a train. They hold each other’s shoulders. Every child tells who is before them and who is after them. The singer says that no one is before them. Meera is after the singer.
keyPoints: The rhyme says, “Here goes our train”.
All the children form a train.
Each child tells who is before and after them.
activities.explanation: Now you know the words, actions, and train positions.

activities.prompt: There are 6 children in the train. The singer is at the front. How many children are after the singer?
steps: The train has 6 children, and the singer is at the front.
Count the children after the singer, giving 5.
The answer is 5 children.

activities.title: A new festival season
activities.body: Uttarayan is a festival in the Indian calendar. Makar Sankranti, Pongal, Bihu, and Lohri are listed with it. It marks the change from winters to summers. Sunny days are returning, and the harvest season is starting. Children celebrate local festivals with their families.
keyPoints: Listed festivals: Makar Sankranti, Pongal, Bihu, and Lohri.
Season change: winters to summers.
Signs: sunny days return and harvest starts.
activities.explanation: This lesson shows what makes the festival season special.

4 + 5 = 9 treats.

activities.title: Celebrations, shapes and patterns
activities.body: Children look at pictures of local festivals celebrated with their families. They discuss the main elements, shapes and patterns. They can extend patterns by drawing further. They can also use concrete objects to make patterns. You can use both ways to explore patterns.
keyPoints: Local festivals are discussed with families.
Celebration pictures show shapes and patterns.
Patterns can be extended by drawing further.
Concrete objects can make patterns.

lessons.title: Shapes, art and India’s heritage

activities.prompt: What secret shapes might you spot in India’s buildings and dances?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Shapes and Beautiful Patterns
activities.body: The world around us is full of shapes. Children are encouraged to appreciate India’s rich heritage. This means noticing beautiful patterns in temples, mosques, churches, gurudwaras and monuments. Children can also explore movement patterns in dance forms. Then they can share what they notice in different art forms.
keyPoints: The world around us is full of shapes.
Beautiful patterns can be explored in many important places.
Children can share what they notice in different art forms.
activities.explanation: Look closely. Shapes and beautiful patterns help us explore art and heritage.

activities.prompt: A temple wall has 6 rows of 5 circle shapes in a pattern. How many circle shapes are there altogether?

6 x 5 = 30 circle shapes.
